deep.reconstruction:
There is no mathematics on this page. It is folio 16 of a set of lecture notes on ancient history, section 'V. Geschichte der Juden', first period, from Abraham to the taking of Palestine (c. 2000 to 1500 BC). The arrangement looks like Heeren's Göttingen lectures on the history of the ancient states. The hand looks like an ordinary student notebook. I cannot confirm that it is Gauss's own writing; it may be notes by a family member or another student kept with his papers.

The content is a narrative paraphrase of Genesis:
- Abraham moves from Mesopotamia across the Euphrates into Palestine, the land watered by the Jordan.
- He separates from his kinsman Lot over pasture. Lot goes south toward Idumaea; Abraham stays in Palestine as a nomad moving among the towns.
- The notes list his nomadic virtues: devotion to family, trust in Jehovah, heroic courage as warrior and victor, and hospitality.
- Isaac's sons Esau and Jacob separate because their herds became too large. Jacob stays and has 12 sons.
- Joseph is the occasion for the family's move to Egypt, about 70 souls.
- They multiply and become first a tribe, then a people.
- The sojourn is given as 430 years by some accounts and 250 by others.
- At the Exodus they number about 1,000,000 souls.

The only quantitative content is these figures: 70 souls, 430 or 250 years, 1,000,000 souls. The following is my own illustration, not on the page. They imply a constant annual growth rate r with 70(1+r)^T = 10^6. That gives r ≈ 2.2% per year for T = 430 and r ≈ 3.9% per year for T = 250. The writer performs no such computation.
errors: No mathematical errors, because there is no mathematics.

Historical and biblical details are as they would be stated in a lecture: Lot is called 'Vetter' (he is Abraham's nephew in Genesis 11:27, 'Brudersohn'). Lot actually settled toward Sodom in the Jordan plain rather than strictly 'Idumäa'. Isaac is called Abraham's 'einziger Sohn', although Ishmael was also his son. These are paraphrase choices or slips of the lecture or note-taker, not mathematical issues.

The figure of 1,000,000 is a common extrapolation from the 600,000 men on foot of Exodus 12:37. The 430 years come from Exodus 12:40. The 215/250-year alternatives come from the chronological tradition (e.g. LXX).

results.what: Narrative summary of the patriarchal period of Jewish history (Abraham to the Egyptian sojourn), with traditional population and duration figures
results.modern_name: Lecture notes on ancient history (Heeren-style 'Geschichte der Staaten des Alterthums')
results.usually_credited_to: Biblical tradition; academic lecture presentation of the period, e.g. A. H. L. Heeren at Göttingen

deep.surprise_reason: This is a non-mathematical history notebook page paraphrasing Genesis. It has no mathematical content and quite possibly is not in Gauss's own hand.

checkable.asserts: (Editorial, not on page) The implied constant annual growth rate from 70 to 1,000,000 over 430 years is about 0.0225, i.e. roughly 2.2% per year.
(Editorial, not on page) The implied constant annual growth rate from 70 to 1,000,000 over 250 years is about 0.039, i.e. roughly 3.9% per year.

transcription_corrections: Line 2: 'vom Jordanstrome[?] durchströmte Land Palästina' is plausible from the image. The [?] can likely be dropped.
'festes[?] Zutrauen zu seinem Jehovah' appears correct.

'bald wurde aus ihnen ein Nomaden[?] und bald eine Völkerschaft': the uncertain word is more likely 'Stamm' ('ein Stamm und bald eine Völkerschaft'). This fits the next page's 'Der Stamm theilte sich'.
'Gastfreiheit[?] zeigte seinen Charakter[?]': the reading is plausible; the line ends with 'seinen Charakter'.
The page number at top left is '16' (faint, in pencil).
